papers.summary: We study Zappa--Szép products of multiplicative racks, namely monoids equipped with compatible rack operations. We characterize multiplicative rack structures on Zappa--Szép products of monoids and prove that every exact factorization of multiplicative racks induces a canonical exact factorization of their universal groups. We also establish exact factorizations of groups of units and cancellative quotients, show that reduction modulo units yields a direct product, and obtain consequences for Ore localization. We then generalize Bianchi's construction using augmentations from partially multiplicative racks into arbitrary multiplicative racks and establish a reconstruction theorem for multiplicative racks with suitable unital ideals. We investigate the interaction between unital ideals and exact factorizations, and characterize Zappa--Szép factorizations of generalized Bianchi-type multiplicative racks. Finally, we use a layered central-quotient construction to obtain finite and infinite non-cancellative multiplicative quandles with non-group factors and nontrivial Zappa--Szép actions, all directly indecomposable as monoids.
papers.title: On Zappa--Szép products of multiplicative racks

papers.summary: In $\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{DC}$, the strict Lipschitz order on proper countably complete filters on any fixed ordinal is well-founded. The proof uses transfinite recursion and closure under countable intersections to derive a contradiction from a descending chain. Restricting each filter to the least ordinal it contains yields a set-like well-founded order that compares filters on different ordinals. In $\mathsf{ZF}$, two ultrafilters on the same ordinal are equal if each is nonexpansively reducible to the other. These results answer both parts of Question 9.2.11 in The Ultrapower Axiom.
papers.title: Well-foundedness of the strict Lipschitz order on countably complete filters

papers.summary: In order to bound approximation errors for deep neural networks, we split the problem into two steps: First the selection of optimal infinite width limits for each layer and second an optimal discretization of all layers to obtain finite sized networks. We show that in expectation, the latter problem is equivalently characterized by a layer wise generalization of Barron norms. Moreover, we provide an analysis of the optimization landscape and show that local minima are characterized by an equidistribution principle akin to similar ideas in adaptive spline and finite element approximation.
papers.title: Barron Smoothness for Layers in Deep Neural Networks

papers.summary: We propose and analyze a fully discrete Crank-Nicolson finite-difference scheme for one-dimensional quasilinear Hamiltonian Gross-Pitaevskii equations with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. We establish the existence and uniqueness of numerical solutions and an $H^1$-stability estimate. For sufficiently regular exact solutions, we obtain second-order convergence in both time and space in the discrete $H^1$-norm. The analysis covers the focusing and defocusing cubic nonlinearities and both signs of the quasilinear coefficient $κ$, under a uniform discrete ellipticity condition when $κ<0$. The main difficulty in the error analysis comes from the derivatives introduced by the quasilinear interaction. To overcome this problem, we introduce a discrete action combining the discrete energy and mass, and establish a coercivity inequality in the discrete $H^1$-norm that allows us to control the numerical error. Together with consistency estimates and a discrete Gronwall inequality, this yields second-order convergence. Numerical experiments with bright solitons corroborate the predicted convergence rates.
papers.title: Numerical analysis of a conservative Crank-Nicolson scheme for quasilinear Gross-Pitaevskii equations

papers.summary: In this work, we consider a parameterized version of the classical wave equation that models wave propagation in damaged material. We apply model order reduction to the wave equation using a reduced basis method with the POD-Greedy algorithm. The success of the model order reduction highly depends on the parameter set used in the POD-Greedy algorithm. While a larger parameter set leads to more insight on the behavior of the full order model, it also prolongs the reduction process in the offline phase for constructing the reduced basis. Therefore, subsampling strategies based on Discrete Empirical Interpolation Method, pivoted QR decomposition and Polytope Division Method are applied.
papers.title: Parameter selection procedures for model reduction of a parameterized wave propagation in damaged material

papers.summary: Kernel-based multilevel methods combine compactly supported radial basis functions with a residual correction scheme and are known to converge linearly in the number of levels. In this paper we study an adaptive version of the multilevel method, in which the interpolation on each level only uses those sites at which the residual of the preceding level exceeds a given threshold. Although this method has been proposed some time ago and converges in all numerical tests, a convergence proof has been missing so far. We close this gap. We derive an a priori error bound, an a posteriori error bound valid for arbitrary point selections, and extend the analysis to penalized least-squares approximation and to target functions outside the native space of the kernel. For a variant with an additional check-loop per level, we show convergence with the rate of the classical multilevel method. We illustrate our findings with three numerical examples.
papers.title: Convergence of Residual-driven Adaptive Kernel-based Multilevel Approximation

papers.summary: For a matrix $U \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}$ ($n \ge k$) with orthonormal columns, the Goreinov--Tyrtyshnikov--Zamarashkin (GTZ) conjecture asserts that there exists a $k \times k$ submatrix $U_I$ with $\|U_I^{-1}\|_2 \le \sqrt{n}$. The conjecture remains open for $3 \le k \le n - 3$. The existence of such a submatrix in the case $k = 2$ was proved for $n=4$ by Nesterenko (2023) and recently for general $n$ by Sengupta and Pautov (2026). In this paper, we give a short, elementary, constructive proof of a weighted strengthening of this result, which yields a single-pass streaming algorithm that selects a row pair satisfying the $\sqrt{n}$ bound in $\mathcal O(n)$ operations and $\mathcal O(1)$ auxiliary memory. We further give an explicit matrix representation of all equality cases for $k = 2$ characterized by Nesterenko (2026) and use it to construct a single matrix family on which standard selection strategies (including global and local maximum-volume selection, Bischof--Stewart pivoted QR, column-pivoted QR, and LU with partial pivoting) simultaneously fail to attain the $\sqrt{n}$ bound.
papers.title: Selecting $2 \times 2$ submatrices with optimally bounded inverses

papers.summary: We investigate the behaviour of simple finite-dimensional Lie algebras under finite Galois field extensions. Given a simple Lie algebra $L$ over a field $\mathbb{F}$ and a finite Galois extension $\mathbb{K}/\mathbb{F}$ of degree $n = [\mathbb{K}:\mathbb{F}]$, we prove that if $L$ is isomorphic to a $\mathbb{K}$-Lie algebra $S$ viewed as an $\mathbb{F}$-algebra, then the scalar extension $L \otimes_{\mathbb{F}} \mathbb{K}$ is isomorphic to the direct sum of $n$ copies of $S$. Furthermore, for cyclic extensions of order a prime number, we show that if no such $\mathbb{K}$-Lie algebra $S$ exists, the extended algebra $L \otimes_{\mathbb{F}} \mathbb{K}$ remains simple. This framework provides a general mechanism to transfer structural and classification results across different ground fields. In addition, we examine the centroids of simple Lie algebras, proving that the dimension of the space of centroids is invariant under finite field extensions. As an application, we explicitly determine the structure of the spaces of centroids for simple Lie algebras over finite fields.
papers.title: Galois scalar extension of simple Lie algebras

papers.summary: We determine which members of the twenty-six families of double extension regular algebras of type $(14641)$ in the Zhang--Zhang classification satisfy a polynomial identity. Retaining the scalar twist parameter, we compute the PI degree for twenty-one of the twenty-two families with PI members and give three possibilities for the remaining family. We establish exact primitivity criteria for the nondegenerate members of eight families and show that sixteen families have no primitive members. The proofs use monomial data, normal subalgebras and crossed products of quantum tori. Twisting by a root of unity preserves the PI property, whereas finite order of the double-extension determinant is necessary but not sufficient for an algebra in the list to be PI.
papers.title: Polynomial identities and primitivity in double extension regular algebras of type (14641)

papers.summary: We study a class of not necessarily normalized generalized cluster patterns which are uniquely determined by the initial seed and mutations. For such generalized cluster patterns, we provide the separation formulas for cluster variables and coefficients.
papers.title: Separation formulas for non-normalized generalized cluster algebras

papers.summary: We introduce the square order $\le^\square$ on group invertible matrices, defined by $A^3=ABA$ and $A\le^s B$, where $\le^s$ is the space pre-order. It is the group inverse analogue of the diamond order: $A\le^\square B$ if and only if $A^\#\le^- B^\#$. Using its block representation, we characterize the reverse order law $(AB)^\#=B^\#A^\#$ for $A\le^\square B$. In contrast to the Moore--Penrose case, the conditions $A\le^- B$ and $(B-A)^\#=B^\#-A^\#$ do not characterize the sharp order; instead, they lead to new partial orders between the sharp and square orders. We also develop a framework where the plus order replaces the minus order in Mitra's unified theory. For a map $\mathcal G$ assigning to each matrix $A$ a subset of its inner inverses, we define $A\le^{\mathcal G}_{+}B$ if $A\le^s B$ and $A=PBQ$ for some pair $(P,Q)=(AA^-,A^-A)$, $A^-\in\mathcal G(A)$, whereas Mitra's relation requires $A=PB=BQ$, and $A\preceq^{\mathcal G}_{+}B$ if $A\le^s B$ and $A^-\le^-B^-$ for some reflexive $A^-\in\mathcal G(A)$ and $B^-\in\mathcal G(B)$. When $\mathcal G(A)$ consists of a single reflexive inverse, we characterize the transitivity of $\le^{\mathcal G}_{+}$ in terms of $\preceq^{\mathcal G}_{+}$, and in general we give a sufficient condition for both to be partial orders. For maps defined by the equations of the Moore--Penrose, group, core and dual core inverses, both relations coincide and only nine arise: the plus, diamond and square orders, two new orders based on core inverses, and four further relations. In Mitra's theory, they yield exactly the minus, star, sharp, core and dual core orders and the one-sided star and sharp orders.
papers.title: A square analogue of the diamond order and a unified approach to the plus order

papers.summary: We identify a class of forcings that includes several classical forcings and prove that for all forcings $\mathbb{P}$ in this class the associated equivalence of generics relation $\equiv^{\mathbb{P}}_M$, as defined by Smythe, is a hyperfinite CBER.
papers.title: A family of forcings with hyperfinite equivalence of generics

papers.summary: Given a set of directions $Ω$, we investigate whether the associated directional maximal operator $M\_Ω$ is bounded on $L^p(\RR^2)$, for $p>1$. One can associate to $Ω$ a numerical quantity called its \textit{Perron capacity}. If the latter is finite, then $M\_Ω$ is unbounded on $L^p(\RR^2)$ for $p \geq 1$. In this paper, we generalize a method introduced by D'Aniello, Gauvan and Moonens to compute the Perron capacity of oscillatory sets of directions such as \[ Ω\_{\mathrm{cos}} = \left \{\frac{\cos (n)}{n}\,: n \in \NN^*\right \}. \] In a second part, using geometric arguments, we show that if the Minkowski dimension of $Ω$ is positive, then $M\_Ω$ is unbounded on $L^p(\RR^2)$ for a small range of $p>1$.
papers.title: Necessary conditions for the boundedness of directional maximal operators

papers.summary:
Petermichl's theorem represents the Hilbert transform by averaging a single dyadic shift over dilations and random dyadic lattices. We study how the deformation stability of the lattice-averaged shift, and of a parameter-free feature map $Φ$ built from it in the spirit of Mallat's wavelet scattering, depends on the number $J+1$ of scales. For the Haar generator as well as compactly supported $C^1$ orthonormal wavelets, the covariance error under a deformation $f\mapsto f(\cdot-τ(\cdot))$ is $O((J+1)
orm{τ'}_\infty
orm f)$ without a $
ormτ_\infty$ term, because lattice averaging absorbs the translation part of $τ$ exactly. The deformation defect splits into a first-order Calderón commutator, bounded uniformly in $J$ by the $T(1)$ theorem, and a second-order remainder. On a single lattice, affine warps and $C^{1,δ}$ generators give a lower bound $c\,σ_\eps\sqrt{J+1}-C\eps$ for the defect, with an explicit constant $σ_\eps\ge0$ computed to be positive for sym4 and db4 at three values of $\eps$. Averaging over lattices turns the defect into a Fourier-multiplier quadratic form, yielding $J$-uniform bounds both for affine warps, with a logarithmic loss in the Haar case, and for $C^2$ warps with $C^{1,δ}$ generators, and hence a scale-uniform Mallat-type stability estimate for $Φ$. With the standard child pair, the Hilbert component of the averaged shift nearly cancels for smooth Daubechies-type generators; re-indexing the children by integers restores this component. For Haar and general warps, numerical computations agree with a conjectured $J$-uniform bound.
papers.title: Random dyadic shift scattering: scale-uniform deformation stability and phase-aligned Hilbert multipliers

papers.summary: What does the topos of a higher-dimensional automaton know about its infinite behaviour that its language does not? We write partial HDAs with an infinite run as models of a geometric theory over an intuitionistic metatheory with no choice. The topos of a machine is that of sheaves on its prefixes. The label word of a prefix records the shape and acceptance bit of each cell with the ipomset of each step. Under unique choice these words give a geometric morphism to the label topos of sheaves on label words, which thus records the shapes and acceptance bits that the Büchi language forgets. Machines sharing their Büchi language and their frames can differ over the label topos. The bouquet of two squares shares its frame and its Büchi language with the interleaved square; each accepted run of either reads the two events in parallel forever. Only the interleaved square has runs through cells of shape a, and the geometric sequent excluding such runs separates the two over the label topos. Over alphabets with decidable equality, finite rigid machines are unambiguous exactly when their label maps are inclusions of locales, and their equivalence over the label topos is decided whenever either is unambiguous. Equivalences of frames over the label topos transport points with their labels, and the invariants of fibres and of the language of points follow from this transport. On finite partial HDAs over alphabets with decidable equality, Muller and Büchi acceptance coincide exactly under a weak form of excluded middle.
papers.title: Higher-Dimensional Automata in Geometric Logic

papers.summary: In this article, we establish an oscillatory sparse domination for the bilinear forms associated with Calderón-Zygmund operators. We further characterize this oscillatory sparse domination in terms of either the boundedness of $T1$ or local endpoint Orlicz norm estimates. Our method also applies to recover Lerner's Sobolev-type inequality in \cite{L2026}.
papers.title: A sparse bilinear form with mean oscillations

papers.summary: The martingale averaged Fourier extension theorem holds for the paraboloid in n dimensions on the Knapp line. Using embedding and interpolation, this gives the complete range of possible exponents (the diagonal case p=q was obtained in [Saw7] using smooth Alpert wavelets instead). OpenAI has recently announced proofs of the deterministic analogue on the diagonal p=q [Ope] and of the local smoothing conjecture [OpeLS], in all dimensions. Since a deterministic estimate at a point on the Knapp line implies the probabilistic one there, the point of the present paper is a short, elementary and self-contained proof of the probabilistic estimate, which uses no Kakeya-type input. We give an application of the probabilistic Knapp theorem to the global initial value problem for the Schrödinger equation, in which we obtain sharp regularity results averaged over martingale transforms of the initial data f.
papers.title: Martingale averages, Fourier extension and the Schrödinger equation

papers.summary: We prove that all abstract classes equipped with an independence relation satisfying a mild local character condition are stable. We obtain the result by using methods from model theory and set theory. We have several applications in the context of abstract classes of modules. In particular, we prove that if $K$ is a class of $R$-modules closed under isomorphisms and pure submodules and $λ^{\operatorname{card}(R) + \aleph_0} = λ$, then $K$ equipped with pure embeddings is stable in $λ$.
papers.title: Stability in abstract classes via set theoretic techniques

papers.summary: We prove that, for every fixed s\in (0,\infty), the set of area s maximizing the weighted sum of the first two eigenvalues of the associated Toeplitz operators on the Fock space must be a disc, up to translations and sets of measure zero. To do so, we first prove the existence of maximizer sets. Then we show that every maximizer set must be a perturbation of a disc when the weight is sufficiently small. Finally, we use the vector-valued version of the analytic implicit function theorem and the inverse function theorem to conclude that the perturbation must vanish when the weight tends to zero.
papers.title: A Perturbative Two-Eigenvalue Faber-Krahn Problem for the Gaussian Short-Time Fourier Transform

papers.summary: We introduce $\mathrm{G3QRC}_1$, the first Gentzen-style sequent calculus for Borges and Joosten's Quantified Reflection Calculus ($\mathrm{QRC}_1$). As a strictly positive, first-order modal logic, $\mathrm{QRC}_1$ crucially escapes Vardanyan's $Π^0_2$-completeness theorem for quantified provability logic, while remaining arithmetically complete with respect to Peano and Heyting Arithmetic. The central innovation of $\mathrm{G3QRC}_1$ is a pair of context-erasing modal rules that simultaneously account for the monotonicity and transitivity axioms by deliberately discarding parametric context across modal boundaries. This structural bottleneck allows for a clean proof of cut-admissibility via a standard lexicographic induction, circumventing the complex loop-checking typically required for provability logics. Cut admissibility yields an instantiated subformula property and supports a direct canonical proof of the finite model property. We streamline the adequate Kripke semantics by interpreting constants globally. We also establish a split-context Craig interpolation theorem and a contextual form of left uniform interpolation, uniformly eliminating private predicate symbols, constants, and free parameters. Finally, by leveraging the rigid structural constraints of the context-erasing rules and the absence of left-branching connectives, we prove that, over the standard fixed countable signatures specified in the paper, the decision problem for $\mathrm{QRC}_1$ is $\mathbf{NP}$-complete, situating this quantified modal logic in a comparatively low nondeterministic complexity class.
papers.title: A Sequent Calculus for the Quantified Reflection Calculus $\mathrm{QRC}_1$: Cut-Elimination, Interpolation, and NP-Completeness
